synopsis: Chapter 6 and the glossary warn that mean average precision (mAP) can be misleading: broader synthetic coverage can raise detector scores even when synthetic and real domains differ, a concern attributed to the 2024 Instance Performance Difference paper [f4818, f12842, f14795]. In the cited on-road Clear2Fog evidence, synthetic-fog pre-training followed by real-fog fine-tuning improved mAP by at most 0.0117 over a real-only baseline [f4448, f4896, f12843, f12917, f14705]. For generative editing as test evidence, vision-language-model jury studies report that edited images match real images, while training-transfer studies report a remaining gap; the corpus cites Clear2Fog’s small gain alongside this tension [f5079].
